problems: Nothing does the chipping: in storyboard frames 4, 7, 10 and 13 a burst of grey cubes flies off the stone, but no tool, hand or beak touches it. The two big clawed feet at the top stay where they are, so the chips seem to come from nowhere.
No knock can be seen. Between chips nothing strikes the stone and nothing marks a sound or a note, so the caption's 'knocked after each chip' and 'each note' are not in the pictures.

The change in shape is hard to see. At 25%, 50% and 75% the stone is a long grey loaf with a slightly deeper waist each time, but at this size and in flat light the dent is only a soft shadow. A viewer can't tell 'four times' or how the shape changed.
A white rectangle (paper or card) appears on the grass beside the left foot from frame 8 on, and it can be seen at 50% and 75%. Nothing brings it there and nothing explains it.

The chips fly much too far. In frame 7 they spray up past the feet at the top of the frame, and by 75% the cubes cover the whole ground. That is far too much debris for a small dent and looks like a particle burst, not stone flaking.
The caption says 'beach stone', but the stone sits on two red-brown logs on green grass. Nothing in the frames looks like a beach.
The frame cuts off the creature that owns the feet, so we only ever see its toes. The left foot slides and smears in frame 16, and the last frame turns darker for no clear reason.
posts.critique: We see a grey stone on two logs throwing off bursts of cubes on its own while a white sheet appears beside it. The chipping, the knocking and the notes the caption promises can't be seen. As a film it reads as unexplained particle effects, not a stone being shaped and tested.
